newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 7.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian Football League team Brisbane was hit by a report last night which claimed Lions player Chris Johnson pushed a field umpire during the team's 18-point win over Richmond at the Gabba yesterday. Umpire Tim Shearer alleges Johnson unduly interfered with him during the first quarter. Page 19.

Australian rugby union centre Pat Howard will be forced out of Australia's next five Test matches due to an ankle fracture and ligament damage, and will undergo surgery in Brisbane today. Australian coach Greg Smith says the lose of Smith will be one of sveral changes to the team in preparation for the next Test match against England. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Australian soccer team has defeated New Zealand 2-0 at Parramatta Stadium, securing the Socceroos a place in the next and final phase of the World Cup campaign. Ned Zelic and Graham Arnold were the goal-scorers. Page 26.

Australian Rugby League club St George has pledged to fight to the bitter end following ARL chief executive Neil Whittaker's statement that clubs should see the reality of merging. A meeting last Thursday saw all clubs receptive to the idea, with the Gold Coast saying they are ready to hold talks on the issue. Page 29.

The Australian under-20 women's basketball team were narrowly defeated by Russia 66-63 in the first stage of their defence of the world championship title at Natal, Brazil. At the conclusion of regulation time the scored was level at 58-58, but the Russias proved stronger in the overtime period. Page 31.
THE AGE

Australian Football League coach Kevin Sheedy has had his contract secured with Essendon for at least 18 months following an announcement by club president Graeme McMahon prior to Essendon's 63-point win over Melbourne yesterday at the Melbourne Cricket Gound. The reassurance follows the club's six straight losses and a subsequent slide down the ladder. Page S2.

Amidst speculation that she was not performing to the best of her form, Australian runner Cathy Freeman ran this year's fastest 400-metre time in Oslo on Friday night. Completing the race in 49.39 seconds, Freeman is now a strong chance to win gold at the world championships in Athens next month. Page S17.

Holden Team racing driver Peter Brock has won round eight of the Shell series at Barbagallo Raceway in Perth yesterday despite the varying weather conditions. The victory was Brock's first for the season and puts him equal fourth behind leader Glenn Seton Page S19.
THE HERALD SUN

The Melbourne Tigers basketball team has defeated Illawarra 102-93 in only their sixth win of the season at Illawarra's Snakepit. The Tigers seem to be regaining form following a bad start to the season. Page 80.

In preparation for Saturday's Grand National Steeple race, New Zealand's Broadway Lad will fly into Melbourne today. Broadway Lad is trained by Kevin Myers and may be a surprise leading contender for the race. Page79.

Sydney Swans Australian Football League coach Rodney Eade was threatened with an indecent language charge after spectators complained to police at the Swans game against Fremantle on Saturday night. The police monitored Eade over a 26-minute period during which he uttered more than 20 expletives. Page 86.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Inadequate refereeing has created public empathy which is said to have helped Auckland defeat Cronulla 11-8 in the Super League match at Ericsson Stadium in Auckland yesterday. Local referee Phil Houston's failure to register forward passes, a crucial error and the enforcement of the 10-metre rule detracted from the Auckland victory. Page 37.

Australian Rugby League team Manly defeated South Queensland Crushers 46-12 at Brookvale Oval yesterday. Manly's four-try hero Terry Hill was almost replaced before scoring his first try after his serious groin injury began troubling him. Page 44.

Canberra Raiders Super League player Brett Mullins will miss tonight's game against Canterbury, to be held at Bruce Stadium, after spending the last week in Canberra Hospital with an abscess in his throat. The Raiders are looking for a return to form after last week's loss to the Hunter Mariners. Page 44.
